SPIKE COMPLETE. Findings: DATE/DATE_AND_TIME/TIME_OF_DAY have zero interpreter support today (confirmed). All three are 32-bit/uint, mirroring TIME's boxing: DATE/DT = seconds since 1970-01-01 epoch, TOD = ms since midnight (range 0..86399999). Comparison is exact equality, no delta, confirmed against upstream FB_TestSuite.TcPOU (AssertEquals_DATE/_DATE_AND_TIME/_TIME_OF_DAY all use <> with no Delta param). Scope for gd2.13 (~7-9 files, same shape as completed gd2.3 TIME/LTIME work): Token.cs (3 new token types), Lexer.cs (3 new word branches + new digit/-/:/. char-class scan loop, distinct from TIME's digit+letter loop), new DateTimeLiteral.cs (YYYY-MM-DD / HH:MM:SS[.mmm] / combined parsing -> uint), Expr.cs (3 literal Expr classes), Parser.Expressions.cs + Engine.Expressions.cs (3 case arms each), Engine.Defaults.cs (0u default), Engine.SizeOf.cs (3x size=4 entries), ScalarAssertType.cs (3 registry entries, WrapUInt-based exact compare like TIME). One open design decision for gd2.13: raw uint vs calendar-string failure-message formatting (upstream uses DATE_TO_STRING/DT_TO_STRING/TOD_TO_STRING calendar formatting, not raw numbers) - current TIME/LTIME precedent uses raw integers, gd2.13 should decide. Gotchas noted: DT has no ms precision despite uint width matching TIME; uint epoch-seconds overflows ~2106 (acceptable); TOD upper bound 86399999ms needs enforcing; single-letter D# literal prefix collision risk is same accepted pattern as existing T#/LT#. No source files modified (read-only research).

Full end-to-end DATE/DATE_AND_TIME/TIME_OF_DAY support: new DateTimeLiteral.cs parser (D#/DATE#, DT#/DATE_AND_TIME#, TOD#/TIME_OF_DAY# literals, uint representation per gd2.12 spike - epoch-seconds for DATE/DT, midnight-ms for TOD), lexer/parser/engine wiring, default values, SIZEOF entries, and 3 new ScalarAssertType registry rows (exact WrapUInt compare, no delta, raw-uint formatting per documented decision). AssertEquals_DATE/_DATE_AND_TIME/_TIME_OF_DAY work via the existing gd2.11 registry-driven dispatch with no NativeMethodBridge changes needed. Value model: keep tree-based Cell model as default. Use escape analysis - any variable with ADR(x) taken anywhere gets allocated in a real flat byte store (TwinCAT layout rules); everything else stays tree-based. Scope: address-taken locals + VAR fields first; skip globals until needed. Boundary is a hard rule: a held pointer dereferenced outside the escaped set, or arithmetic on a non-escaped variable, throws unsupported-construct at the throw site - never a silent/best-effort value (this is exactly the case the failure taxonomy exists for; a silent approximation would let TcAgent "fix" a false negative).

Fact-check during grilling: existing single-call MEMCPY/MEMSET/MEMMOVE round-trip (Engine.ByteLayout.cs) already reuses SizeOfType's alignment/pack_mode math, so it's internally consistent for named-variable-to-named-variable copies - "rebuild everything on a flat buffer" was overbroad. But internal consistency isn't TwinCAT conformance (pack and SIZEOF agree by construction, which can't catch a wrong rule) and four single-call cases likely still diverge from real TwinCAT even without escape analysis:
- interior/out-of-bounds ADR (MEMCPY past a buffer's end) - pick a policy (favor hard error over silent truncation) and document it
- partial-field writes (copy count not aligned to field boundaries) - must not silently vanish
- MEMCPY overlap on one named variable (e.g. ADR(arr[0])/ADR(arr[2]) with overlapping ranges) - pack/copy/unpack via a separate buffer accidentally gives MEMMOVE semantics; must implement true MEMCPY (overlap-incorrect) semantics
- count expressions that aren't SIZEOF of either operand

Root cause was NativeCallContext.TryGetArg (Extensibility/NativeCallContext.cs), not ArgBinder/BindParams - BindParams already binds named-then-positional calls correctly via ArgBinder.TryResolveArg. 3. Field naming unified: suite-level errorKind -> kind, errorConstruct -> construct. One vocabulary (kind/construct) at every JSON level - top-level error, suite-level error, per-test failure. Breaking rename from today's three-name inconsistency.

4. parse-error JSON shape pinned: kind: "parse-error". Reuses existing line/bodyLine fields for position - no new position field. The offending token (required by TcXunit-229.6's "carrying the offending token and line") is carried in the now-unified construct field rather than a new dedicated token field - one field for "the identifier/text that characterizes this failure" regardless of kind.

5. Inline agent directive, uniform across all five kinds - every message is self-contained actionable guidance an agent can act on without ever reading the README, no docs-only carve-outs:
   - assertion: fix the code under test or the expectation
   - plc-fault: real runtime defect, fix the code under test
   - unsupported-construct: STOP, escalate as a grammar gap, never rewrite the POU to make it pass (retrofit - today this guidance lives only in doc comments/README, not the message text)
   - load-error: check file/path/XML/discovery, not about the code under test (retrofit - today raw exception passthrough)
   - parse-error (new): open the cited line; fix if genuinely malformed; STOP and escalate if it looks like valid ST

Decision recorded in the DESIGN field: (1) Latin-1 is the assumed narrow encoding, per Beckhoff's documented default, and a code point above U+00FF raises instead of silently truncating; {attribute 'TcEncoding':='UTF-8'} is a named out-of-scope gap since nothing parses pragmas. (2) Both capacity and content are byte-measured - that is a fact, not a choice - and under Latin-1 the two coincide; content lands in 2o9.6, capacity enforcement split out as 2o9.9 because the Cell carries no declared type. (3) One shared helper in the interpreter beside StringByteCell, consumed by Engine.Get/SetStringByte, ByteLayout pack/unpack, and CharacterMeasure.Narrow. Primary-sourced, and it corrected the premise: within Latin-1 one byte IS one code unit, so the narrow measure was already right and 2o9.6 rescoped from 'make it byte-counted' to 'guard the range and unify the paths'. Two beads filed from what surfaced: 2o9.8 (WSTRING sized n+1, TwinCAT says 2*(n+1), wrong alignment too) and 2o9.9 (STRING(n) capacity unenforced).

Commit 9f9f666. TEST-ONLY as fenced - git status showed only the new file, no production change. New tests/xStunit.Interpreter.Tests/Conformance/LayoutChecklistPackWriteTests.cs (6 tests). Method: a holder FB declares src : <fixture type> plus a 64-byte dest poisoned to 16#FF, then MEMCPY(ADR(dest), ADR(src), SIZEOF(src)) routes through PackCellToByteView into a SizeOfType-allocated buffer; the view width is measured SEPARATELY through the plugin boundary (NativeCallContext.RequireBytes), the one caller that bounds-checks the packed view.

THE MEASUREMENT - SizeOfType and the pack write AGREE on all three fixtures:
ST_TrailingPadding  SIZEOF 8  - fills wide 0-3, tail 4; padding 5-7 zero; view width 8, a read of 9 refused with only 8 byte(s) available.
ST_WideAlignment    SIZEOF 32 - fills leadIn 0-3, wideFloat 8-15, wideInt 16-23, trailer 24; padding 4-7 and 25-31 zero; view width 32, 33 refused.
ST_ArrayStride      SIZEOF 28 - elements at 0/8/16 each 4+1 content bytes, sentinel 24; padding 5-7/13-15/21-23/25-27 zero; view width 28, 29 refused.
In every case dest bytes from SIZEOF to 63 were still 0xFF, so the copy touched exactly SIZEOF bytes and not one more.

RULE PINNED IN PROSE: a pack write fills the declared fields into a freshly zeroed SIZEOF-sized buffer. Padding is never carried over from the source (the interpreter has no storage for it), so it reads as ZERO at the destination and CLOBBERS whatever the destination held there. A SIZEOF-byte MEMCPY is a whole-type copy, padding included - not a copy of the field bytes alone. That is the input xstunit-229.28 was waiting on.

THE ONE REAL OBSTACLE, an interpreter gap not a shape question - filed as xstunit-2m7k. Engine.Clock has NO ST-visible advance (driven only from C#, StepCycles is time-agnostic, wiki/03 says so outright), so a TcUnit suite sees time frozen at zero and cannot watch a TON fire. Interpreter NOT touched - outside the fence. Coverage split instead: the ST suite pins both ENDS exactly (at DebounceTime 0 the windows are empty so Active tracks the level cycle for cycle in both directions; at any non-zero DebounceTime no window can ever close so an edge is held however many cycles it is presented), and the C# timing tests pin what is strictly between (release exactly at DebounceTime - 19ms no, 20ms yes; a sub-window glitch restarting rather than resuming; meters ignoring a swallowed bounce). EVERY miniload module with a timer will need the same split until 2m7k lands, S2 FB_Conveyor included.

THREE JUDGEMENT CALLS FOR PATRICK - the doc names the six-member surface but not the wiring underneath, so these are mine and deliberately cheap to overturn: (1) Simulation : BOOL as the override selector, because SimulatedInput alone cannot express override-active and ST has no null; (2) HardwareInput : BOOL as the field-bit VAR_INPUT name; (3) ST_SensorDatas member list - the doc names the type but not its fields, so it is the value view of the published surface plus RawLevel (the selected source before polarity, which is what commissioning compares against the terminal LED). S2 needs it as ARRAY[1..5] OF ST_SensorData, so S2 is where a different member list would show up. FOURTH: TimeActive/TimeInactive measure the CURRENT UNBROKEN STRETCH and reset on transition rather than accumulating a lifetime total - elapsed accumulators admits both readings, and current-stretch is what a blocked-conveyor or lane-clear diagnostic needs. Stated in the interface prose so the choice is visible rather than buried.

Ran the CLI against the real fixture project this was reported from and found the
actual failing assertion. Root cause: a FUNCTION_BLOCK's own top-level ST body only
runs when the FB itself is invoked - nothing implicit triggers it. The fixture's
"host" FB wires its VAR_INPUT interface reference down onto a nested "builder" FB
only inside its own cyclic body, but the failing test never invokes that body (only
plain public methods), so the nested field stays at its unassigned default even
though the host's own field was set directly. A VAR_IN_OUT-forwarded reference into
a nested method then correctly evaluates the null-check as FALSE - matching the real
IEC 61131-3 semantics, not diverging from them. This would fail identically in real
TwinCAT/TcUnit given the same source, so no live-hardware run was needed to confirm
branch 3 of the acceptance criteria.

A literal past 64 bits is now a ParseException naming the literal, from the lexer for the based form (keeping the original 16#... spelling, which the token text loses) or the parser for decimal, replacing a bare OverflowException out of int.Parse and, for based literals, a silent unchecked wrap that had been surfacing as the nonsense diagnostic 'Cannot assign negative value -1 to a ULINT/LWORD variable'. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA DEVIATION, stated rather than papered over: the 'no new MemberSize/MemberOffset/TypeSize rows' clause is NOT met for PlcTaskSystemInfo. Sizing OTCID lets the comparison walk further into TwinCAT's own system-info types and into a hole the .tmc never describes - declared members stop at bit 256 (RTViolation) and TaskName is declared at bit 512, the 32 bytes between being a reserved array TwinCAT keeps out of the symbol description - so MemberOffset PlcTaskSystemInfo.TaskName and TypeSize PlcTaskSystemInfo are displaced by definition on both targets. NumericCoercion.CoerceForAssignment now narrows a long or int back to uint when the target cell already holds one, so a TIME value read from C# is the same box whether or not arithmetic touched it - (uint)Fields['TotalRunTime'].Value succeeds exactly as it does on a timer ET, and the Convert.ToUInt32 workaround in the miniload fixture engine is gone along with the comment explaining it. CoerceForAssignment is the right site because it is the single choke point every assignment form funnels through - SetVariable, field, GVL field, array element and both Engine.Defaults initializer paths - and the only place that knows the destination; Promote sees operands only. Working from the box in the cell is sound here specifically because TIME/DATE/DT/TOD are the only IEC types boxing as uint, so 'existing is uint' identifies the family unambiguously. The behavioural half was settled in the same pass, as the acceptance criteria required: the narrowing is deliberately unchecked and WRAPS. TwinCAT stores these types in 32 bits, so a sum past T#49d17h2m47s295ms rolls over and a negative difference rolls under; rejecting the overflow would make xStunit stricter than the machine it stands in for. Both wrap directions are pinned, and the rule with its reason is written at the coercion site. TOD, DATE and DT share TIME's box and are fixed by the same rule; LTIME already boxed correctly as ulong and is pinned so the rule is not over-generalised onto it. UDINT/DWORD were probed and deliberately left: they already box as long so the box is right, and what they lack is 32-bit wrapping, which cannot be done here because UDINT, DWORD and LINT are indistinguishable once boxed as long - filed as xstunit-2o9.19. A neighbouring hole found in the same path was filed rather than folded in: LTIME mixed with TIME throws NotSupportedException out of Promote's ToULong, which has no uint case, as xstunit-2o9.18. Does not touch xstunit-ubtw's long/ulong hole - this fix adds only long-to-uint and int-to-uint. 10 tests added.
